I've written the full NFL audit, about 6,500 words of text plus tables. It's based on 2,160 seeded simulated games run through the real drive and play engine, plus browser checks at 390, 430, 320 and 844 landscape. The repo is unchanged, the port-5202 server is stopped, and the existing 65 football tests pass.

"Human proxy" below means the repo's human-pace autopilot model (a weaker passer that reads and throws 1.5–2.9 s after the snap).

Top findings:

1. **Critical: the ball carrier stops dead after a catch or handoff unless the stick is already held** (`engine.ts:785-797`).
   - In the live game, 5 of 5 catches without the stick braked to zero within 0.25 s and lost yards.
   - In simulation, a 0.35 s reaction drops yards per carry from 3.9 to 1.2, yards after catch from 5.7 to 2.0, and points per game from 13.9 to 9.1.
2. **Critical: the play-call panel hides your own team before the snap.** At 390 and 430 the QB and RB are covered; at 320 all 11 players and the line of scrimmage are; in landscape the passing panel covers the RB and slot. Run plays show no lane on the field.
3. **High: difficulty is unfair to the player.** The same difficulty setting also applies to your defense, so on Rookie the human proxy wins only 47.5%. The AI throws in about 1.5 s and is almost never sacked on Legend (0.1%), while the human proxy is sacked 26.6% of the time.
4. **High: top-tier games collapse.** Elite squads on Legend (the online setting) score 4.9 points a game with 6.9% interceptions and turnovers on 31% of drives. One game in five ends tied, and ties are decided by squad rating.
5. **High: runs have no big plays.** Only 7–12% of runs lose yards (NFL about 18%) and 0–3% gain 10+ (NFL about 11%). Even the 99th-percentile run is under 10 yards, and the three run plays differ by under half a yard.
6. **High: deep passes are too easy for a person.** The human proxy gains 20+ yards on about 19% of throws (NFL about 8–9%) and completes about 60% of deep balls (NFL about 35–40%).
7. **High: the WR2 card barely matters.** It gets about 5% of targets in AI play. Flipping the formation or swapping the cards doesn't change it, so the play designs are the cause, and that card does almost nothing in sims and takeovers.
8. **High: no pocket control.** The QB can't move, the only escape is an irreversible RUN IT, there's no throwaway, and sacks have no animation.
9. **High: thin defense and playbook.** The defense is always two coverages behind a four-man rush, with no blitzes or situational calls. The offense is one formation with 8 pass plays and 3 runs.
10. **High: animation gaps.** Juke, spin, stiff arm and truck use hand-made poses (the juke is the basketball crossover pose), even though motion-capture cut and stiff-arm clips exist unused. The QB slides back in an idle clip, and there are no get-ups or returns.
11. **High: match structure.** Head-to-head and UT matches have no pause or quit, ties have no overtime or two-point try, and you never see or influence the opponent's drives.
12. **High: everyone looks the same.** All 22 players share one skin tone with no hair or gear, and draft fill-ins are labelled like "WR 81". This is the owner's "who is who" request.

The audit also covers medium issues: camera framing, kick meter, punt being a useless option, missing box score, stale copy and hints, the playbook dialog overflowing the screen, HUD overlaps, ability pop noise and render costs. Frame rate holds 60 fps, and 57 fps at 4× CPU throttle with a few hitches. It ends with what to keep, a fix order, and which fixes need the NFL protocol bump (draft 10→11, UT 11→12).

Files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/`:
- audit-nfl.md
- audit-shots/nfl/
- audit-scripts/ (scripts and raw sim output, nfl_* files)

I've written the full audit of the NBA engine and controls, with 30 findings ranked by severity. Two are critical and eleven high. All of it is measured from seeded autopilot games against real Ultimate Team squads, the existing human-strategy harness, the rating curves, and touch-driven Playwright captures at five iPhone sizes. Nothing in the repo was changed (`git status` clean, existing hoops2 tests 41 passed and 2 skipped), and the port 5201 server is stopped.

1. **Critical: it's a score attack, not a basketball game.** You play 16 offense-only possessions and never defend. The rival's score is simulated before tip-off and revealed as you play (`Arcade.tsx:196,243-250`). Finals land around 20–18, a game lasts 2–2.5 minutes, and 5–10% of games tie and are decided by squad rating.
2. **Critical: you can't tell players apart.** Everyone has the same skin tone and hair colour, with a hair style hashed from the player ID (`render.ts:61-77`), so ten players differ only by jersey number.
3. **High bug: the shot clock on screen freezes.** It only updates when something else redraws the HUD; I measured it stuck on "8" for 7 seconds before the violation fired (`Hoops2.tsx:784`).
4. **High bug: a thumb already on the stick at tip-off is ignored for the whole possession** (`Hoops2.tsx:619-621`). Reproduced: the knob stayed centred for 2.25 s of live play.
5. **High: small phones hide your own player.** At 375×667 and 320×568 the ball handler is under the CROSS / STEP BACK / PASS buttons. The SCREEN / CUT / SPACE calls sit about 600 px from either thumb, and at 320 wide the move buttons overlap the LAST PLAY button.
6. **High: the stats aren't NBA-like** (NBA figures in brackets):
   - Free-throw rate is 0.02 (0.24), because nothing but an and-one is ever fouled.
   - Mid-range shots go in 65% (about 42%), and team effective FG% is 61% (54.7%).
   - Turnovers run 6.6% of possessions on Pro and 18% on Legend (about 12%).
   - The best-rated player scores only 7.5–16% of team points, while one player takes about 62%.
   - Elite-shooter AI squads shoot after 2.6 s: 83% threes, 89% heavily contested.
   - Era behaviour runs backwards: 2000s and 2010s squads shoot more threes than 2020s squads.
7. **High: the green window is smaller than the input can resolve.** An average shooter gets ±17.5 ms, and the floor is ±3 ms. Release timing uses the 60 Hz game clock rather than the touch event, the green slice is drawn 1–4 px wide, and a "PERFECT" release under a heavy contest still misses 38–68% of the time.
8. **High: animation.** Feet visibly slide on 29% of on-ground frames. Recorded crossover, dribble, jump and catch clips exist but are unused. The step-back is the crossover played backwards, and blocks, rebounds and contests share one pose.
9. **High: camera.** The view from behind the shooter hides the on-ball defender behind your own man and pans the shooter under the buttons on every shot. Near the rim, players and labels pile into an unreadable stack.
10. **Medium:**
    - Banner text covers the rim on every make, block and call.
    - The pixel font drops accented letters ("JOKI ") and "&".
    - One difficulty setting drives both defenses, so the Legend AI scores less than the Pro AI (18.6 vs 20.5 points).
    - Simple human tactics manage 0.4–0.9 points per possession against the AI's 1.17–1.28, even on Rookie.
    - There's no pause or quit and no end-of-game box score, and iOS haptics are one delayed tick for everything.

Performance is fine (about 2 ms a frame normally, about 10% of frames over 16 ms at a 4× CPU slowdown). The deterministic engine, physical rebounds, recorded jump shot, rating tests, landscape layout and render-only effects layer should be kept. The audit closes with a fix order and notes which fixes need the NBA online protocol bumped from 10 to 11; most of the input and layout fixes don't.

Scripts, logs and screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/audit-scripts/` and `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/audit-shots/nba/`.

Files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/`:
- `audit-nba.md`

The audit is written: 1 critical bug, 3 critical design problems, 9 high findings, plus medium and low items, all measured. I opened 10,000 seeded packs of every pack type in all three sports, plus 26 Live Calendar packs, and took phone screenshots. Nothing in the repo was changed.

**Critical**
- **Bug: Spotlight (100–105) and GOAT (106–110) cards sell for 30 coins (NBA) or 10 (NFL).** The sell-value function overwrites their price with the bronze one (`packs.ts:504-517`). SBC auto-fill then picks them as the cheapest card: in a test it put a registered 104 Michael Jordan Spotlight into a Bronze Upgrade for a Silver pack, and the confirm screen gives no warning.
- **The Scout Market sells two 94–97 "Hot Season" cards every day** for about 2,100 coins (NBA) or 1,500 (NFL) (`market.ts:27-33`). That is 45× cheaper than pulling one from Premium packs, so the long-term chase ends within about two weeks.
- **Rarity runs backwards against rating.** Hot Season (94–97) is a permanent pool of 518 NBA / 1,106 NFL cards and is the cheapest chase card. Legends (88–94) are the rarest, at roughly 177k–310k coins expected. A 3,500-coin Spotlight pack gives a 100+ card 20% of the time, which beats the year's 98–99 Finale.
- **Hot Season cards show numbers the match doesn't use.** A bronze 59 NFL season becomes a 94 whose card shows THP 99, while the match uses THP 79. 115 NFL Hot Season cards are built on bronze or silver seasons.

**High**
- **Preview Pack:** its one-hour cooldown (none after a buy) lets a player buy only Premium packs that hold a special, at 1,800 coins instead of about 27,100 per special.
- **Admin store packs:** the admin store packs undercut the once-a-week Standout Guarantee with no limit; NFL Captains costs 1,000 against 1,800.
- **Live program packs:** they cost almost the same as their guarantee packs (3,000 vs 3,200 NBA), so the program pack is never worth buying.
- **Soccer:** it gets NFL-position SBCs that can't be completed ("Pass Catchers: WR WR TE", "Skill Set"). The existing sport-branch test doesn't catch the `nba(c) ? … : …` pattern behind them.
- **Odds sheets:** they show tiers only, with no odds by overall rating and no holo odds. The Scout's Choice sheet is wrong.
- **Promo presentation:** promos have no hub page and no launch moment. A program card's walkout says "PROGRAM" and the reveal headline says "8 golds".
- **Live Calendar:** about half of it isn't built. Check-in stamps, Season Path, extra pass tiers and surprise flash windows exist only in the JSON, and soccer has no calendar.
- **Promo sets:** they're flat and repetitive. Whole promos land at one rating, and Michael Jordan '88 appears in 8 program editions.
- **Weekly Standouts:** they're random seasons, and an 82 still gets a full walkout with confetti.

The rest of the report has the measured odds and value tables per pack and sport, the promo uplift table, coin earn rates and days to afford each pack, SBC reward values, a comparison with real Ultimate Team packs, a fix order with the online queue bumps needed when ratings change, and a list of what already works and must be kept.

Files are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/`:
- `audit-packs-promos.md` (the report)
- `audit-shots/packs-promos/` (screenshots)
- `audit-scripts/` (scripts; data in `audit-scripts/out/`)

The audit is written at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/audit-soccer.md` (about 7,000 words including tables). It draws on 1,600 seeded matches, about 3,000 scripted-player attacks, probes and phone-size screenshots; the repo is unchanged and the 5203 server is stopped.

**Critical**
1. **You never defend or see the opponent.** A match is the same 7 attack set-ups every time (`match.ts:52`). The AI's attacks are simulated off-screen and its goals appear silently in the scoreboard (`Soccer2.tsx:772`).
2. **The portrait camera shows only 16.9 m of the 68 m pitch width.** At kick-off 0–1 of your 3–5 teammates are on screen, so passes go to men you can't see. In every wide overload your own player starts off-screen (x = −36 / 426 px), his name tag stuck behind SPRINT. Landscape looks right, but the app is locked to portrait.
3. **A no-skill strategy wins.** Sprint straight at goal and hold SHOOT at 16 m with no aim: this scores 58.5% of counters, against 20% for the built-in AI. It also wins a free kick or penalty on up to 30% of runs.
4. **Card ratings act like a cliff for the player.** The same run against a 78-rated defence scores 1.7% with 70-rated attackers and 92.3% with 90s (`tackleWin`, `ratings.ts:115`).

**High**
- **Frozen ball:** a shot that stops short of goal can't be touched and stops the clock, so the attack hangs for up to 120 s. This happens in 0.83% of attacks.
- **Keepers parry into their own net:** 14.3% of all goals come straight from a parry (`engine.ts:1062` sends it toward the goal line).
- **Shot numbers are off real football:**

  | | Game | Real |
  |---|---|---|
  | Shots per side | 5 | 12–13 |
  | On target | 53% | 33–35% |
  | Converted | 20% | 10–11% |
  | A player shooting from 30 m | 16–22% | ≤2% |

  The scorelines themselves (2.3 goals a match, 26% draws) are realistic.
- **Difficulty is flat or inverted:** the AI scores 1.17 a match on Rookie and Pro and 0.99 on Legend.
- **Free-kick BEND buttons are reversed:** "Bend left" curls the ball 3.4 m right.
- **No reward for aiming:** aim assist beats a deliberate corner aim (49% vs 40%), and there are no chip, finesse or driven shots.
- **Thin animations:** one right-footed kick for every pass and shot, a belly-flop for keeper dives and slide tackles, no dribble touches, skill moves or get-ups.
- **Every player has the same skin and hair colour** (`render.ts:79-80`), which is what the owner's "who is who" request is about.
- **On-screen overlaps:**
  - The first hint covers the goal and the aim reticle.
  - "FREE KICK" and "BEND" print over each other as "FBENDICK".
  - The opponent's penalty taker gets your yellow control ring.
  - Corner shots spend 37% of the screen on sky and stands.

**Medium:** sprint is on the right thumb, the joystick is fixed, there's no pause, and the UT formation is ignored by the engine. The match plays the NFL crowd instead of the soccer sounds, the opponent's goals throw confetti in your colours, the shootout keeper only picks a direction beforehand, and the final screen is bare.

**Keep:** the deterministic seeded engine and ball physics, the bounded ratings, realistic AI-vs-AI scorelines, the 2026-11-02 aim/shoot/pass controls with miss reasons, the keeper model, offside and the shootout rules. Performance is fine: 60 fps normally, hitches at 4–6× CPU slowdown.

Any engine fix needs the soccer queues bumped: draft 2 → 3 and UT 2 → 3.

Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/audit-shots/soccer/` and the scripts with their outputs in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/audit-scripts/`.

The audit is written. The owner's blurred, faded header comes from iOS 26, not from our CSS, and a fix is drafted but can't be confirmed outside the owner's iPhone. I walked every screen in all three sports at 393×852, 430×932 and 320×568 (9 walks, 748 screenshots), with zero page errors, no overflow and no cut-off text on any screen.

**The header problem (critical)**
- **Measured from the owner's screenshot:** above about 80 pt the "LEVEL 19" text is about 35% darker and 4× softer than "510/620 XP", which is the same colour lower down. A blur plus dimming band runs from the top of the screen to about 22 pt below the status-bar inset.
- **Our CSS doesn't draw it:** no element in the top band has any blur, mask, filter or transparency. Chromium renders the same layout, matching the owner's photo point for point, and it is sharp.
- **Cause:** iOS 26 blurs and dims a band under the status bar on home-screen apps, and no CSS can turn it off. Every header, toast, the pack SKIP button and the in-game score bug start only 6–17 pt below the inset, so their top halves fall inside that band.
- **Fix:**
  - **Required:** add a top clearance of `min(22, inset × 0.4)` in `src/stage-layout.ts` and `stage.tsx:151` (`--sat`), and the matching rule on `.arcade-full`. A runtime test moved all header content clear, but NBA/NFL Home then scroll about 22 px, so it ships with the Home hint fix (M1).
  - **Recommended:** a solid fixed bar behind the status area in `index.html`; it may stop the blur, but only a device test will tell.
  - I reproduced the owner's look and checked the fix by injecting CSS in the browser; the screenshots are under `edge-*`. The final check is a screenshot from the owner's phone.
- **"Cut off":** nothing is cropped sideways. The blur band eats the top of the level ring and the LEVEL label. Separately, on NBA/NFL Home the hint line under the modes sits beneath the PLAY bar's shadow and looks cut.

**Other high findings**
- **Card detail buttons float mid-sheet on every notch/Dynamic Island iPhone** (`nav.css:1120` ignores the bottom inset), so card stats show through below them. It's a one-rule fix.
- **Every player shares one skin tone and hair colour** (`body.ts:591`), drawn from behind. Jordan has hair, and 20 Jordan cards look identical. This misses the owner's "know who is who" request; the fix direction is a per-player appearance table.
- **Card art is flat:** every gold card is the same, card text is 3–9 px, some team badges are as low as 1.25:1 contrast, and the pack art is generic.
- **Main Home never shows UT rewards:** the UT tab badge only says "FREE" before the starter pack, even with 6 rewards and 2 packs waiting.
- **Objectives, Missions and Gauntlet are dead ends:** "IN PROGRESS" is a disabled chip with no button to go play it.
- **Mode names copy EA FC's** (Ultimate Team, Squad Battles, Rivals, SBC, Evolutions, Moments), and card details link to "2K"/"Madden" references. The brief requires our own names; the owner should decide.
- **Top cards show walls of 110s** (Brady: five identical maxed stats), which reads as fake.

**Notable medium findings**
- **Squad Battles vote screen:** every solo Squad Battles, Legends Events and Moments game shows the online "HEAD TO HEAD · SIM OR PLAY?" screen with a 10-second countdown.
- **Collection filters:** LANDMARK, PROGRAM and STANDOUT always show 0 editions.
- **Soccer draws:** a 2–2 draw is shown as a WIN.
- **Thin progress screens:** the results screen and the Season Pass give little sense of progress.

The report also covers the missing engagement hooks, what works well and must be kept (navigation, the UT Home hub, odds and the Pack Tracker, pack opening, Daily), and a suggested fix order. Nothing in the repo was changed, nothing live was contacted, and the port-5205 dev server is stopped.

Sources for the iOS 26 behaviour: [WebKit bug 301756](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=301756), [301108](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=301108), [301994](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=301994), [316008](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=316008)

Full audit written to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/overhaul/audit-likeness-animation-perf.md (about 7,000 words). I changed no repo files, and the 5206 servers are stopped.

Top findings:

1. **Critical, likeness.** Every player in all three engines and on every card has the same skin tone (`#a8714f`) and hair colour (`body.ts:592-611`). Hair and beard are chosen by hashing the player id, which gives wrong looks: bald Iverson, high-top Shaq, dark-haired Haaland, bearded Mbappé. With everyone in the same kit, 12 NBA stars differ only by height (`lineup-nba.png`).
2. **High.** Weight barely changes the drawn body. At the same scale Shaq (325 lb) and Manute Bol (200 lb) both get a 20 px torso. Soccer has no weight data, and the match and the card each invent a different formula for it.
3. **High.** Height, weight and number are the only appearance data for the 19,938 Ultimate Team players. There is no skin, hair, accessories, handedness, preferred foot, era look or kit pattern.
4. **High.** Every card shows the same tiny standing figure: about 52 CSS px tall on the club grid, with a head about 8 px across. Draft cards show initials on a jersey. Numbers vanish or scramble when a player is turned, and 26% of NFL cards have no number.
5. **Critical (NFL), animation.** Each frame may draw only 4 new sprites, and that budget is spent on the far players first. In NFL autoplay 41% of player draws show the previous frame's sprite, rising to 81% for the nearest, largest players. The near defenders and backfield freeze and slide. NBA close-ups are affected 8.4% of the time.
6. **High.** No animation blends into the next. Pose jumps at a switch are 22–60% of body height, against 11–18% for a normal frame step.
7. **High.** Dunks (the windmill arm never circles), the crossover, spin, pass and block, and the NFL juke (which reuses the basketball crossover pose), stiff arm and truck are hand-made poses, not motion capture. Five of the 26 recorded clips are never played: dribble, crossover, cut, stiff arm and get-up-from-front.
8. **High.** Every player in every sport uses the same jump shot, throw, right-footed kick and celebration.
9. **Medium.** Most clips play at 15 fps and small sprites at 10 fps. Soccer feet slide on 12.8% of player frames.
10. **High, performance.** Opening Ultimate Team takes 2.1 s at desktop speed and 7.4 s (NBA) / 9.0 s (NFL) at 4× CPU slowdown. It has long tasks up to 669 ms and keeps an extra 41–57 MB of memory for the session.
11. **High.** Ultimate Team fails offline ("The cards didn't load") unless it was opened online on the current build. Meanwhile the install still caches 3.2 MB of Ultimate Team-only rating data, even for soccer players.
12. **Medium.** Every launch has a splash floor of at least 1.15 s, plus a render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet and up to a 2.2 s font wait. Font loading was blocked by the isolation, so that cost comes from the code rather than a measurement. An offline relaunch took 3.9–4.0 s to reach Home in all three sports.
13. **Medium.** Matches hold 60 fps at normal speed on every viewport tested. At 4× CPU slowdown NBA drops to 51.8 fps at 430 px wide, with frame times up to 50 ms. A cold first visit is 2.2–2.6 s to interactive at 4× CPU on 4G, with 603–785 KB of JS (gzip). The install cache has grown to 11.5 MB from the 8.79 MB recorded in the performance doc.

Already good, and worth keeping: the code-drawn rig, the motion-capture pipeline (event timing, retargeting, mirrors, the build script), speed-matched running, rendering kept out of the simulation, iOS canvas-memory care, in-match name tags, and flat memory over 40 s of play. All the fixes above are rendering-only and need no protocol bump, as long as simulation timing doesn't change.
